channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold consolidates below $4,300 as hawkish Fed, higher bond yields and bullish USD weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its consolidative price move through the Asian session on Friday and languishes near the weekly low set the previous day amid a bearish fundamental backdrop.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: At make or a break near 1.1350
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades marginally lower at around 1.1375 against the US Dollar (USD) in the early European trade on Friday, but is inside Thursday’s trading range. The major currency pair is broadly under pressure as the US Dollar (USD) outperforms across the board.

item.title: Swiss Franc trades near 16-month lows as US Dollar surges on hawkish Fed expectations
item.description: USD/CHF extends its gains for the third consecutive day, trading around nearly 16-month highs of 0.8296 during Asian hours on Friday. The currency pair appreciates as the US Dollar (USD) strengthens, driven primarily by hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar remains depressed around 0.5650, near June lows vs bullish USD
item.description: The NZD/USD pair attracts sellers for the third straight day, flirting with its lowest level since late June, around mid-0.5600s during the Asian session on Friday. Spot prices remain on track to register losses for the fifth straight week and seem vulnerable amid a bullish US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Indian Rupee cushioned by RBI’s likely intervention, outlook remain fragile
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains a temporary ground against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday after remaining under pressure in the past few days. The USD/INR pair struggles to extend gains above 95.96 on the likely Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) intervention.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Softens to near 1.3200, staying bearish under 100-day SMA
item.description: The GBP/USD pair trades in negative territory around 1.3210 during the early European session on Friday. The British Pound (GBP) weakens against the US Dollar (USD) amid growing domestic fiscal concerns ahead of the upcoming UK budget.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices fell in India on Friday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Slips below $92.00 amid Iran diplomacy hopes; bullish potential intact
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – extends the previous day's late pullback from the $95.80 area and drifts lower through the Asian session on Friday.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Weakens to near 111.00 as bearish technical bias holds below 100-day SMA
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross attracts some sellers to around 111.10 during the early European session on Friday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) edges higher against the Australian Dollar (AUD) as traders remain on high alert for currency intervention from Japanese authorities.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Tests nine-day EMA support near 180.00
item.description: EUR/JPY has pared back its recent gains from the previous day, trading around 180.10 during Asian hours on Friday. Technical analysis of the daily chart shows that the currency cross continues to trade within a descending channel pattern, pointing to a persistent bearish outlook.

item.title: United States Dollar Index approaches 101.80 as bond yields keep rallying
item.description: The US Dollar continues to outperform its peers as United States (US) Treasury Yields keep rallying due to firm expectations of more interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve (Fed) in the near term.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD remains steady near $94.00 as oil prices ease
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) inches higher after two days of losses, trading around $63.90 per troy ounce during Asian hours on Friday. Non-yielding Silver is finding underlying support as inflation concerns ease following a pullback in crude oil prices.

item.title: Japanese Yen recovers from three-week low vs USD amid looming intervention risk
item.description: The USD/JPY pair drifts lower during the Asian session on Friday, stalling its recent strong move up to a three-week high, near the 159.00 mark, touched the previous day.

item.title: Australian Dollar flatlines near 0.7000 as traders assess Trump-Xi summit
item.description: The AUD/USD pair holds steady around 0.7010 during the early Asian trading hours on Friday. Traders continue to assess the developments surrounding the US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping summit at the White House.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama says BoJ's latest rate hike was done to achieve inflation target
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister (FM) Satsuki Katayama said on Friday that the latest rate hike from the Bank of Japan (BoJ) was done to achieve the inflation target. Katayama added that she expects the central bank to conduct appropriate monetary policy while coordinating with the government.

item.title: Canadian Dollar weakens amid falling oil prices, stronger US Dollar
item.description: USD/CAD extends its gains for the fifth consecutive day, trading around 1.4140 during Asian hours on Friday. The pair appreciates as the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) faces downward pressure from falling crude oil prices.

item.title: British Pound consolidates above 1.3200, its lowest since late June against a bullish USD
item.description: The GBP/USD pair edges higher during the Asian session on Friday, trading above its lowest level since June 29, around the 1.3200 neighborhood, touched the previous day.

item.title: Euro posts modest lossess on rising Fed hike odds, Middle East tensions
item.description: The EUR/USD pair trades with mild losses near 1.1375 during the early Asian trading hours on Friday. The US Dollar (USD) strengthens against the Euro (EUR) amid hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve (Fed) officials and a lack of progress between the US-Iran talks.

item.title: WTI drops to near $92.50 on potential US-Iran deal
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price declines after two days of gains, trading around $92.60 per barrel during Asian hours on Friday.

item.title: China's President Xi says Beijing and US should seek new ways for major countries to coexist
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping stated during his visit to Washington that Beijing and Washington must find a proper way to coexist peacefully and act as partners rather than rivals, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.

item.title: Saudi Civil Defence issues warning over possible threat in Jazan
item.description: Yemen's Houthi claimed on Thursday that it launched dozens of ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi military installations in the kingdom's southwestern Jazan region, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said were aimed at Taif in western Saudi Arabia and the Yanbu area on the Red Sea.

item.title: Iran’s President says US ‘must choose’ whether to end war
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said that it is for the United States (US) to decide whether to end its war against the Islamic Republic, as Tehran does not wish to continue fighting, Fox News reported on Thursday.

item.title: Gold declines below $4,300 as rising oil prices and hawkish Fed stance dampen appeal
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) declines to near $4,275 during the early Asian session on Friday.

item.title: Japanese Yen keeps sliding as Tokyo repeats its warning and holds fire
item.description: Finance Minister Katayama said on Thursday that the principles behind the joint US-Japan intervention of July 31 are still alive, and USD/JPY went on to touch 159.00, its highest since early September. The pair is trading just under 159.00, on track for a fifth straight gain.

item.title: Australian Dollar tests 200-day SMA amid soaring US yields
item.description: The Aussie Dollar fell for the third straight day, down 0.37% against the US Dollar, which remained boosted by elevated US yields, which jumped as Oil prices rose and as inflation pressures built. The AUD/USD trades at 0.7012, near the 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) of 0.7021.

item.title: Mexican Peso : Range view with downside risks against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s USD/MXN analysis highlights recent moves driven by Oil-related Dollar strength and heavy speculative long-MXN positioning.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar grinds lower as US bond yields climb to new highs
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) has its Official Cash Rate (OCR) at 2.75%, and markets now price at least a 75% chance that it goes to 3% on October 28, against about 30% right after the September 2 hike. NZD/USD is trading just above 0.5650, its lowest since late June.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average falls a third day as bond yields climb
item.description: The 30-year Treasury yield touched 5.50% on Thursday, and two Fed officials gave bond buyers no reason to expect relief. New York Fed President Williams said another rate increase this year looks reasonable, and Philadelphia Fed President Paulson said rates may need to rise a little more.

item.title: Pound Sterling slides again as Fed speakers go full hawkish
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) Deputy Governors Lombardelli and Breeden said on Thursday that they are moving closer to voting for a rate hike, and the Pound fell for a fourth straight session regardless. GBP/USD is trading just above 1.3200, its lowest in nearly three months.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: BI prioritizes IDR stability – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Henry Hao and Moses Lim report that Bank Indonesia kept the BI Rate at 5.75% while expanding FX hedging incentives to support the Indonesian Rupiah. Governor Destry Damayanti signaled a preference for non-rate tools and incentive-based measures over SRBI yield hikes.
